newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - Utilicorp, PECO launch EnergyOne.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Utilicorp, PECO launch EnergyOne.

text.p: Electricity utilities Utilicorp United Inc. and Peco Energy Co. said Tuesday they were launching a one-stop-shopping service for a variety of utilities. A new jointly-owned company, EnergyOne L.L.C., will offer natural gas and electricity services, as well as AT&T Corp. residential communication services and ADT Ltd. home and business electronic security offerings.
A full text of the company's press release follows.

WASHINGTON--June 24, 1997-- Anticipating radical restructuring of the electric utility industry, UtiliCorp United and PECO Energy Company today broke new ground by announcing the formation of EnergyOne, L.L.C., the industry's first nationwide branded energy marketing company designed to speed the benefits of competition to other utilities and consumers.

Operating as a separate enterprise, EnergyOne is an ambitious effort to fundamentally change the way electric and natural gas utilities relate to their customers by integrating traditional energy offerings with a portfolio of competitively-priced products and services under the EnergyOne(sm) label.

EnergyOne will market AT&T residential communication services and ADT's home and business electronic security offerings. EnergyOne, L.L.C. is an expansion of a national branding concept introduced by UtiliCorp United in 1995.
Also joining in today's launch of EnergyOne are AT&T Solutions which will establish and manage an integrated national call center and billing system.

The $310 billion electricity and natural gas utility industry is undergoing significant change brought on by a convergence of deregulation, the introduction of new technologies, and the expected entry of experienced non-utility retailers into what has long been considered a staid monopoly business.

EnergyOne, L.L.C. serves as the management clearing house responsible for developing relationships with suppliers, evaluating and selecting new products and services, and establishing competitive wholesale pricing mechanisms. Participating utilities serve as retail distributors of the products, drawing upon EnergyOne's national marketing identity and support.

Founding partners UtiliCorp and PECO Energy each hold a 50 percent equity interest in EnergyOne, L.L.C. and are the initial retail distributors. EnergyOne obtains revenues from franchise, royalty and transaction fees from participating distributors and suppliers.

Andrew M. Guarriello, president and CEO of Kansas City-based EnergyOne, compared the initiative to other marketing entities like Century 21 in real estate, True Value Hardware stores and banks offering nationally branded credit cards.

"By joining EnergyOne, participating utilities will be strongly positioned to retain customers, compete more effectively in a new energy marketplace, and stake a claim on the leading edge of an entirely new business category -- integrated utility services," Guarriello said.

UtiliCorp United Chairman and CEO Richard C. Green, Jr. said that he expects other utilities across the country to join EnergyOne when they realize how it can help them avoid the significant expense required to develop similar marketing, product and customer support systems on their own.

"One of the keys to successfully meeting customer expectations in the new competitive marketplace will be effective control of expenses to lower unit costs. EnergyOne offers participating utilities a cost-effective opportunity to accelerate their local marketing efforts with the power of a tested and proven national brand," Green said.
Corbin A. McNeill, Jr. president and CEO of PECO Energy, emphasized that the EnergyOne concept also is a "win-win" for both energy users and suppliers.

"Residential and business customers will save money as the result of competitive pricing, convenience and a wider choice among quality offerings, while suppliers gain access to a larger customer base," McNeill said.

Other EnergyOne officers are Paul K. Morris, executive vice president of marketing and sales; and Roderick C. Mack, executive vice president of products and services. A former Long Island Lighting Company marketing executive, Morris also held sales and marketing positions with IBM and Exxon. Mack gained extensive technology management experience while serving at AT&T, Mastercard and Sprint.

Based in Kansas City, UtiliCorp United is a $4.5 billion international electric and gas company with energy customers and operations across the U.S. and in Canada, Great Britain, New Zealand, Australia and Jamaica. The company operates regulated electric and gas utilities in eight states and one Canadian province, and is among the six largest-volume wholesale marketers of natural gas and electricity in the U.S.

PECO Energy Company, based in Philadelphia, Pa., is the 15th largest electric and natural gas utility in the U.S., one of the largest generators of power and one of the leading marketers of wholesale power in the U.S. With 7,200 employees, $15 billion in assets, and $4.3 billion in annual revenues, PECO Energy provides retail utility service to 1.5 million electric customers and nearly 400,000 natural gas customers in southeastern Pennsylvania. PECO Energy also markets nationally wholesale energy services, power plant operations and management, infrastructure management, telecommunications, and a package of customized energy solutions to business and institution customers.
